# Independent audit: truncated-triangle tilted boundary concentration

Source read in full:
`candidate 1b1d5e313c1943d1`,
Sections 1--5. Verdict: PASS. Companion checker rerun: 3,094 exact checks PASS.

The coordinates (x,y)=(ts,t(1-s)) have Jacobian t. Polynomial division gives
the exact Z and I formulas, and I-bZ=V is correct. The logarithmic primitive
has derivative (s+b)log s, with both lower-end terms tending to zero.
Thus c_m tends to exp(1/2), Z_m to 1+log 2, and I_m to 1/2.

The row rho=dm/(Z ell) has the displayed actual mean and marked value
cV/Z, so both the tilted contact identity and the original uniform-row
identity are exact. The prescribed-mark global parameter inequality follows
from ordinary Jensen under bar_rho, followed by concavity under rho. It is
correctly separated from deepestness or a physical minimum.

All explicit geometry bounds in Section 3 check, including the coordinate
lower bound 63/512, diagonal lower slack 31/256, upper slack 1/7 and the
uniform radius 1/32 source ball. The harmonic-number maximum bound and
reciprocal total-mass bound are applied with the correct normalization.

In the weak-limit decomposition, the first term has density dm/(x+y)
and total mass one. The second has mass tending to log 2 and vanishing mass
outside every fixed neighborhood of the origin. Uniform continuity of a
test function gives precisely the stated atom. The normalization factors
in both measures (14), and the distinct tilted/original limiting means,
are correct.

The limiting source admits a cap fraction 1/[4(1+log 2)^2], well below
the triangle centroid depth 4/9. Thus the counterexample does not provide
a deepest source and does not disprove nonconcentration under that extra
physical hypothesis. Finally integral |grad log L_m|=sqrt(2)Z_m is bounded:
this confirms that scaled surface-log vanishing is entirely consistent
with the surviving unscaled reciprocal-density atom.

No correction is requested. This is an exact obstruction to automatic
uniform integrability under bounded parameters/source cores/contact rows,
not a counterexample to the full mixed-depth variational problem.
note: Mathematical discussion retained to expose corrections and limitations. This is not a verification run, accepted premise, or approval of the revised submission. Association follows explicit source-document references, not an inferred dependency.
